newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario Hydro sets massive nuclear overhaul.
newsitem.headline: Ontario Hydro sets massive nuclear overhaul.

text.p: Provincially owned Ontario Hydro, North America's largest power utility, unveiled on Wednesday a massive overhaul of its troubled nuclear power operations, including a temporary shutdown of seven nuclear units.
Ontario Hydro Chairman Bill Farlinger told a news conference that four units at Pickering, Ontario and three units at Bruce, Ontario would be shut over the next year. A
heavy water plant at Bruce will be permanently shut down.
Farlinger said that the cost of the shutdown and overhaul of other operations could cost between C$5 billion ($3.6 billion) and C$8 billion ($5.8 billion) over five years, starting in 1997.
In addition, Ontario Hydro is considering writing off C$2 billion ($1.44 billion) in assets this year.
Ontario Hydro said it would replace the electricity generated by the laid up units by operating existing fossil-fuel plants at higher levels and bringing back mothballed units.
"This overhaul will not affect rates. We will uphold Hydro's current mandate to meet all the electricity supply needs of our customers," Farlinger said in prepared remarks for the news conference.
He said extensive upgrades would also be made at the utility's Pickering and Bruce B units and Darlington plant.
